title: PostgreSQL 16 max_connections Exhausted Under Pooling
short_description: Resolve FATAL 53300 too many connections on PostgreSQL 16 pools.
content:
## Symptom

Application logs show `FATAL: 53300 too many connections for role "svc_app"` and new connections are rejected on PostgreSQL 16.

## Root Cause

The `svc_app` role exhausts its per-role connection limit before PgBouncer pooling absorbs the burst.

## Resolution

Raise the role limit and verify pooled usage:

```sql
ALTER ROLE svc_app CONNECTION LIMIT 200;
SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE usename = 'svc_app';
```

Reload configuration without restarting:

```bash
psql -U postgres -c 'SELECT pg_reload_conf();'
```

title: PostgreSQL 14 max_connections Exhausted
short_description: Resolve FATAL 53300 too many connections on PostgreSQL 14 instances.
content:
## Symptom

PostgreSQL 14 rejects client connections with `FATAL: 53300 too many connections`.

## Root Cause

Server-wide `max_connections` parameter reached on standalone PostgreSQL 14 without proxy pooling.

## Resolution

Edit `/etc/postgresql/14/main/postgresql.conf` and raise `max_connections`:

```bash
sed -i 's/max_connections = 100/max_connections = 300/' /etc/postgresql/14/main/postgresql.conf
systemctl restart postgresql@14-main
```

title: PostgreSQL Transaction ID Wraparound Danger and Autovacuum Starvation
short_description: Prevent forced database shutdown when transaction ID age exceeds autovacuum freeze max age.
content:
## Symptom

PostgreSQL server logs emit `WARNING: database "prod_db" must be vacuumed within 10000000 transactions` followed by potential read-only lock.

## Root Cause

Long-running analytical queries or orphaned replication slots prevent autovacuum from advancing `relfrozenxid`.

## Resolution

1. Identify blocking locks and replication slots:

```sql
SELECT pid, age(backend_xmin), query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE backend_xmin IS NOT NULL ORDER BY age(backend_xmin) DESC LIMIT 5;
SELECT slot_name, active, xmin FROM pg_replication_slots WHERE active = false;
```

2. Run manual aggressive vacuum freeze on oldest tables:

```sql
VACUUM FREEZE ANALYZE verbose public.incident_logs;
```

title: PostgreSQL Deadlock Detected on Concurrent Batch Inserts
short_description: Mitigate ERROR 40P01 deadlock detected during concurrent batch transactions.
content:
## Symptom

Application transactions abort with `ERROR: 40P01: deadlock detected` during simultaneous bulk updates.

## Root Cause

Competing worker threads update records in differing primary key ordering, resulting in circular lock dependency.

## Resolution

Enforce deterministic sorting of primary keys before transaction batch execution:

```sql
-- Application query pattern: order IDs deterministically
SELECT id FROM incidents WHERE id IN (101, 45, 89) ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE;
```
Tune deadlock detection timeout in PostgreSQL:
```sql
SET deadlock_timeout = '2s';
```

title: PostgreSQL WAL Disk Space Starvation During Heavy Ingestion
short_description: Recover from PANIC: could not locate a valid checkpoint record due to full pg_wal partition.
content:
## Symptom

PostgreSQL crashes with `PANIC: could not locate a valid checkpoint record` and `No space left on device` on `/var/lib/postgresql/data/pg_wal`.

## Root Cause

Failing archive command (`archive_command`) or lagging replica causes unarchived WAL segments to accumulate.

## Resolution

1. Temporarily allow archiving bypass or fix destination disk space:

```bash
df -h /var/lib/postgresql/data/pg_wal
psql -U postgres -c "SELECT archived_count, failed_count, last_failed_wal FROM pg_stat_archiver;"
```

2. Use `pg_archivecleanup` to safely purge recycled WAL files:

```bash
pg_archivecleanup /var/lib/postgresql/data/pg_wal 000000010000012A00000045
```

title: Redis OOM Command Not Allowed Under Memory Limit
short_description: Fix OOM command not allowed when maxmemory limit is reached on Redis cache.
content:
## Symptom

Redis returns `OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'` on write commands (SET, HSET).

## Root Cause

Default `maxmemory-policy` is `noeviction` and keys are written without expiration TTL.

## Resolution

Change eviction policy to `volatile-lru` or `allkeys-lru` dynamically:

```bash
redis-cli CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru
redis-cli CONFIG SET maxmemory 4gb
```

Audit top memory-consuming keyspaces:
```bash
redis-cli --bigkeys
```

title: Redis Memory Fragmentation Evicts Celery Workers
short_description: Diagnose Redis fragmentation above 1.5 evicting Celery broker keys.
content:
## Symptom

Celery workers lose their broker connection while `INFO memory` reports `mem_fragmentation_ratio:1.87`.

## Root Cause

Jemalloc allocator retains uncompacted memory pages after rapid burst creation and deletion of task messages.

## Resolution

Enable active defragmentation on Redis 7:

```bash
redis-cli CONFIG SET activedefrag yes
redis-cli CONFIG SET active-defrag-ignore-bytes 100mb
redis-cli CONFIG SET active-defrag-threshold-lower 10
```

title: Redis Sentinel Failover and Split-Brain Following Partition
short_description: Resolve split-brain dual masters in Redis Sentinel clusters after network partitions.
content:
## Symptom

Client writes succeed on two differing master nodes simultaneously, leading to silent data loss during failover.

## Root Cause

`min-replicas-to-write` and `min-replicas-max-lag` are unset, allowing isolated master to accept writes without quorum.

## Resolution

Configure minimum replicas on all Redis master configs:

```bash
redis-cli CONFIG SET min-replicas-to-write 1
redis-cli CONFIG SET min-replicas-max-lag 10
```

Verify sentinel master status:
```bash
redis-cli -p 26379 SENTINEL master mymaster
```

title: Redis Replication Buffer Overflow Causing Full Resync Loop
short_description: Fix infinite replication reconnect loop when client-output-buffer-limit slave is exceeded.
content:
## Symptom

Redis replica disconnects repeatedly with logs: `Client id=... scheduled to be closed ASAP for overcoming of output buffer limits`.

## Root Cause

Replica replication buffer (`repl-backlog-size`) is smaller than master write rate during initial snapshot transmission.

## Resolution

Enlarge replication buffer and slave client buffer limits:

```bash
redis-cli CONFIG SET repl-backlog-size 256mb
redis-cli CONFIG SET client-output-buffer-limit "replica 512mb 128mb 60"
```

title: Redis Cluster Slot Migration Hang on Large Hash Keys
short_description: Resolve CLUSTERDOWN Hash slot not serving state during stalled redis-cli resharding.
content:
## Symptom

Cluster commands fail with `CLUSTERDOWN Hash slot not serving` during cluster slot rebalance.

## Root Cause

A hash key with over 500,000 fields times out synchronous `MIGRATE` command across cluster shards.

## Resolution

Inspect stalled importing and migrating slots:

```bash
redis-cli -c cluster nodes | grep -E "importing|migrating"
redis-cli --cluster fix 127.0.0.1:7000
```

title: Celery Worker Task Starvation from Unbounded Prefetch
short_description: Prevent long tasks from starving other Celery workers when worker_prefetch_multiplier defaults to 4.
content:
## Symptom

Queued short tasks wait indefinitely in Redis/RabbitMQ queue while some Celery workers are idle.

## Root Cause

Default `worker_prefetch_multiplier=4` assigns batches of tasks to busy workers running long-duration jobs.

## Resolution

Set prefetch multiplier to 1 and configure acks-late in celery settings:

```python
app.conf.update(
    worker_prefetch_multiplier=1,
    task_acks_late=True,
    task_reject_on_worker_lost=True,
)
```
Restart celery workers with concurrency tuning:
```bash
celery -A app.core.celery worker --concurrency=4 -Ofair
```

title: Celery Worker Lost on Child Process SIGKILL Under Memory Pressure
short_description: Diagnose WorkerLostError caused by Linux OOM killer terminating Python child processes.
content:
## Symptom

Celery job logs report `billiard.exceptions.WorkerLostError: Worker exited prematurely: exitcode 137 (SIGKILL)`.

## Root Cause

Cumulative memory leaks in Python dependencies accumulate over thousands of task executions until Linux OOM killer fires.

## Resolution

Enable worker task recycling and memory limits in Celery configuration:

```python
# Recycle worker process after executing 500 tasks
app.conf.max_tasks_per_child = 500
# Recycle worker if resident memory exceeds 500 MB
app.conf.max_memory_per_child = 500_000
```

title: RabbitMQ High Memory Watermark Alarm Blocking Publishers
short_description: Unblock publisher connections when RabbitMQ hits vm_memory_high_watermark alarm.
content:
## Symptom

Producers hang indefinitely on `channel.basic_publish()` and RabbitMQ logs say `memory resource limit alarm set on node`.

## Root Cause

Erlang broker process consumes greater than 40% of host RAM due to unacknowledged messages or queue backlog.

## Resolution

Inspect broker alarm status:

```bash
rabbitmqctl status | grep -A 5 alarms
rabbitmqctl list_queues name messages_unacknowledged consumers
```

Temporarily raise memory watermark threshold or purge abandoned dead letter queues:
```bash
rabbitmqctl set_vm_memory_high_watermark 0.6
```

title: NGINX 502 Bad Gateway from Uvicorn Socket Queue Overflow
short_description: Resolve 502 Bad Gateway connect() failed (111: Connection refused) under peak HTTP traffic.
content:
## Symptom

NGINX returns `502 Bad Gateway` to HTTP clients. Error log shows `connect() failed (111: Connection refused) while connecting to upstream`.

## Root Cause

The Uvicorn application backlog queue (`--backlog 2048`) is saturated and Linux kernel `somaxconn` drops incoming SYN packets.

## Resolution

1. Increase OS socket listen backlog:

```bash
sysctl -w net.core.somaxconn=4096
echo "net.core.somaxconn=4096" >> /etc/sysctl.conf
```

2. Scale Uvicorn worker count and set matching backlog:

```bash
uvicorn app.main:app --workers 8 --backlog 4096 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
```

title: NGINX 504 Gateway Timeout During Upstream Slow Query Degradation
short_description: Mitigate 504 Gateway Time-out upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) on NGINX proxy.

title: NGINX SSL Handshake Failure Due to Expired Certificate Chain
short_description: Fix SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL or certificate expired errors on NGINX reverse proxy.
content:
## Symptom

Browsers and API clients fail connection with `SSL certificate problem: certificate has expired` or `SEC_ERROR_EXPIRED_CERTIFICATE`.

## Root Cause

Let's Encrypt or corporate TLS certificate reached expiration without automated certbot renewal reload.

## Resolution

1. Renew certificate with certbot:

```bash
certbot renew --force-renewal
```

2. Verify certificate expiration date:

```bash
openssl x509 -enddate -noout -in /etc/letsencrypt/live/api.example.com/fullchain.pem
```

3. Test NGINX configuration and reload:
```bash
nginx -t && nginx -s reload
```

title: Legacy Apache HTTP Server KeepAlive Worker Exhaustion
short_description: Legacy Apache 2.2 prefork MPM worker starvation on long persistent HTTP connections.
content:
## Symptom

Server ceases accepting new connections with `server reached MaxClients setting, consider raising the MaxClients setting`.

## Root Cause

Obsolete Apache 2.2 prefork architecture holds dedicated OS process per idle keep-alive connection.

## Resolution

Decommission legacy Apache proxy and migrate traffic to NGINX reverse proxy with event-driven architecture.
For emergency mitigation:
```apache
KeepAlive Off
MaxClients 256
```

title: FastAPI Async Event Loop Blocked by Synchronous I/O Calls
short_description: Diagnose high API response latency and request timeout when synchronous code blocks the asyncio loop.
content:
## Symptom

FastAPI endpoint latency spikes to 10+ seconds for all concurrent requests when one client triggers a heavy report.

## Root Cause

A route declared with `async def` executes synchronous disk file I/O or requests calls directly on the single async event loop thread.

## Resolution

Offload synchronous blocking functions to `asyncio.to_thread` or declare route with standard `def` (which FastAPI runs in threadpool):

```python
# BAD: blocks event loop
# async def get_data():
#     return requests.get("http://slow-api")

# GOOD: run in thread pool
from starlette.concurrency import run_in_threadpool

async def get_data():
    return await run_in_threadpool(blocking_client.get)
```

title: Uvicorn Worker Process Killed on Timeout in Gunicorn Cluster
short_description: Fix CRITICAL WORKER TIMEOUT when Gunicorn kills silent Uvicorn worker process after 30s.
content:
## Symptom

Gunicorn master process logs `[CRITICAL] WORKER TIMEOUT (pid:12345)` and kills worker child, dropping in-flight HTTP connections.

## Root Cause

Database query without statement timeout hangs indefinitely inside worker thread, exceeding Gunicorn's default 30s timeout.

## Resolution

Configure database connection statement timeout and extend Gunicorn worker timeout:

```bash
gunicorn app.main:app -w 4 -k uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker --timeout 120 --graceful-timeout 30
```

In SQLAlchemy/asyncpg engine configuration:
```python
engine = create_async_engine(DATABASE_URL, connect_args={"command_timeout": 20})
```

title: Docker Container Terminated with Exit Code 137 (OOMKilled)
short_description: Investigate and resolve Docker container termination triggered by host cgroup OOM killer.
content:
## Symptom

Container shuts down unexpectedly. `docker inspect <container_id>` shows `"State": {"ExitCode": 137, "OOMKilled": true}`.

## Root Cause

Application memory consumption exceeded the container's strict `mem_limit` defined in `docker-compose.yml`.

## Resolution

1. Inspect memory usage prior to crash:

```bash
docker stats --no-stream
dmesg -T | grep -i oom
```

2. Adjust memory reservation and limit in `docker-compose.yml`:

```yaml
services:
  api:
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 2G
        reservations:
          memory: 1G
```

title: Docker Daemon Inotify Watch Limit Exhausted on Linux Host
short_description: Fix ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers reached in containerized apps.
content:
## Symptom

Services with file watchers fail to start inside containers with `Error: ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers reached`.

## Root Cause

Host Linux kernel parameter `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` is exhausted by multiple container volume mounts.

## Resolution

Increase kernel inotify watch limits on host OS:

```bash
sudo sysctl -w fs.inotify.max_user_watches=524288
sudo sysctl -w fs.inotify.max_user_instances=512
echo "fs.inotify.max_user_watches=524288" | sudo tee -a /etc/sysctl.conf
sudo sysctl -p
```

title: Kubernetes Pod CrashLoopBackOff Due to Failed Readiness Probe
short_description: Resolve CrashLoopBackOff and 0/1 Running status when health probe fails initial check.
content:
## Symptom

Pod status oscillates between `Running` and `CrashLoopBackOff`. `kubectl describe pod` reveals `Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503`.

## Root Cause

`initialDelaySeconds` is shorter than application cold-start time (database migrations + model preloading).

## Resolution

Increase `initialDelaySeconds` and add a dedicated `startupProbe`:

```yaml
startupProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /healthz
    port: 8000
  failureThreshold: 30
  periodSeconds: 5
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /healthz
    port: 8000
  initialDelaySeconds: 10
  periodSeconds: 5
```

title: Kubernetes Node DiskPressure Evicting Application Pods
short_description: Recover from The node had condition: [DiskPressure] causing pod eviction on worker nodes.
content:
## Symptom

Pods enter `Evicted` status across worker nodes. Node describes condition `DiskPressure = True`.

## Root Cause

Container runtime root filesystem or log directory exceeds `imageGCHighThresholdPercent` (default 85%).

## Resolution

1. Prune unused container images and garbage collect docker/containerd:

```bash
crictl rmi --prune
journalctl --vacuum-time=2d
```

2. Verify disk usage on `/var/lib/kubelet` and `/var/log`:

```bash
df -h /var/lib/kubelet
kubectl get nodes -o wide
```

title: Linux Filesystem Inode Exhaustion with Free Disk Space
short_description: Resolve No space left on device errors caused by 100% inode utilization (df -i).
content:
## Symptom

            File writes fail with `No space left on device` even though `df -h` shows gigabytes of available space.

            ## Root Cause

            Millions of tiny files (such as un-cleared session files or email spool) exhaust filesystem inodes (`df -i` shows 100% `IUse%`).

            ## Resolution

            1. Check inode utilization across partitions:

            ```bash
            df -i
            ```

            2. Find directory containing massive file count:

            ```bash
            find /var/spool /tmp /var/log -xdev -printf '%h
' | sort | uniq -c | sort -k 1 -n | tail -10
            ```

            3. Purge orphaned small files using find delete:
            ```bash
            find /tmp/app_sessions -type f -mtime +7 -delete
            ```

title: NFS Mount Stale File Handle Error on Remote Network Storage
short_description: Fix Stale file handle (ESTALE) on NFS network shares after server reboot or inode reallocation.
content:
## Symptom

Processes accessing `/mnt/shared_storage` hang or fail with `ls: cannot access: Stale file handle` (errno 116 ESTALE).

## Root Cause

The remote NFS server rebooted or replaced the underlying exported filesystem, invalidating cached client file handles.

## Resolution

Force lazy unmount and remount the NFS share:

```bash
umount -l /mnt/shared_storage
mount -t nfs -o rw,hard,intr,timeo=600,retrans=2 nfs-server.internal:/export /mnt/shared_storage
```

title: ServiceNow OAuth2 Token Expiry Buffer Failure Causing 401 Unauthorized
short_description: Prevent transient 401 Unauthorized errors during ServiceNow Table API calls on expiring OAuth tokens.
content:
## Symptom

API requests to ServiceNow Table API return intermittent `401 Unauthorized` with `{"error": "invalid_token", "error_description": "Token expired"}`.

## Root Cause

The OAuth client caches tokens until exact `expires_in` seconds, but network transit and clock skew allow the token to expire in flight.

## Resolution

Enforce a 30-second token expiry refresh buffer (`servicenow_token_expiry_buffer_seconds=30`):

```python
# In ServiceNow OAuth client:
def is_token_expired(self) -> bool:
    buffer_seconds = settings.servicenow_token_expiry_buffer_seconds
    return time.time() >= (self._token_expires_at - buffer_seconds)
```

Refresh token immediately if within the buffer threshold before executing Table API HTTP requests.

title: Internal TLS CA Certificate Verification Failure Across Microservices
short_description: Resolve CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED: self-signed certificate in certificate chain errors.
content:
## Symptom

Python clients (httpx, requests) raise `ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] self-signed certificate in certificate chain`.

## Root Cause

The service container uses standard public CA bundle (`certifi`) which lacks the organization's private root CA certificate.

## Resolution

Install organization root CA certificate into system trust store:

```bash
sudo cp /tmp/corp-root-ca.crt /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/
sudo update-ca-certificates
```

Configure Python runtime environment variable:
```bash
export SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
```
